thread:
Alex Chen: Hi @Riley — quick confidential question. Maria asked to swap my desk because of sensory triggers and says my night on-call shift makes it worse. Jamie told me we can't swap because of rotation fairness. I want to be helpful but feel pressured to give up my shift. What are my options?

Riley (People Ops): Thanks for flagging, Alex. We can keep this confidential. Two quick Qs: has Maria filed an accommodation request formally? And are you open to temporary adjustments (noise-cancelling, small desk move) while we sort it out? :thinking_face:

Alex Chen: No formal request yet. I asked Maria yesterday if she wanted to open an accommodation and she said she was 'trying to avoid HR' but really needs a quieter spot. I'm okay with headphones but worried about last-minute on-call changes being expected of me.

Jamie Patel: For context — rotation fairness matters because swapping creates a cascade. That said, we can do a temporary cover agreement rather than change the rotation permanently. I proposed pairing Alex with Sam for the noisy week. I didn't think escalation would happen so fast.

Maria Gomez: I didn't want to drag HR in but my sensory sensitivity has gotten worse. The hum in that corner makes it impossible to focus; nights are hardest. I'm open to temporary coverage but I need a reliable plan. Sorry for putting pressure on you, Alex.

PeopleOpsBot: Reminder — accommodation requests go through the Accessibility & Accommodations intake so we can document, provide reasonable adjustments, and protect confidentiality. https://intranet.redwood.ai/people/accommodations (bot)

Riley (People Ops): Maria — thank you for sharing. If you're comfortable, submit the intake form and we can start the interactive process. For Alex, we will not require unilateral changes. Two paths: 1) Manager-mediated temporary coverage (formalized for X days) or 2) workplace adjustments (desk move, white noise machine, headphones stipend). We can also offer a short mediate conversation.

Alex Chen: That sounds fair. I could do a 3-day swap if it's formal and documented, not just an ask in chat. Would prefer noise-cancelling + slight desk shift otherwise.

Jamie Patel: I'll draft a temporary coverage plan. Quick schedule draft (example):
```
Week A: Alex on-call (cover: Sam covers nights 2-4)
Week B: Alex resumes normal rotation
```
I'll post PD to on-call rota and cc people ops.

Riley (People Ops): Perfect. Next steps: Maria fills intake (link above) — we do a 15-min intake call within 48 hrs, manager (Jamie) proposes temporary coverage doc, Alex confirms availability, and People Ops approves interim adjustments (headphones/desk move) within 72 hrs. We'll keep this confidential except necessary managers.

Maria Gomez: I'll submit the intake form today. Thank you all.

Alex Chen: Appreciate the clarity. Happy to do short swap with the doc. Please keep me in the loop and confirm when it's on the rota. :+1:

Riley (People Ops): Thanks everyone. I'll schedule the intake and ping Alex/Jamie with the meeting invite. If anything changes or you prefer a private DM, ping me directly. :handshake:
